# A CI build (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, and no coding agent in the environment or
# among the ancestor processes) follows branch heads like every other build.
# The first go command of a run that resolves an org module on a branch locks
# that head in the run lock store. Every later go command of the same run and
# attempt builds the locked version, so a commit that lands in the middle of a
# run reaches no job of it. This script points the store at a directory.
#
# The go command cannot make a CI build under an agent, and a script cannot
# prove that no agent started it. So this script runs only where no agent is an
# ancestor of the test. org_branch_head.txt covers the builds outside CI.

[short] skip 'constructs local git repositories'
[!git] skip
[agent] skip 'a coding agent is an ancestor of this test, so the go command never makes a CI build'

env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$WORK${/}home${/}gopher${/}.gitconfig
env HOME=$WORK${/}home${/}gopher
env GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file
env GOPRIVATE=github.com/wow-look-at-my
[!GOOS:windows] exec git config --global 'url.file://'$WORK'/alpha.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'
[GOOS:windows]  exec git config --global 'url.file:///'$WORK'/alpha.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha'
[!GOOS:windows] exec git config --global 'url.file://'$WORK'/beta.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta'
[GOOS:windows]  exec git config --global 'url.file:///'$WORK'/beta.insteadOf' 'https://github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta'

env GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Go Gopher'
env GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='gopher@golang.org'
env GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME
env GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL

# The script engine passes none of these through, and this says so.
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=
env CLAUDECODE=
env GROK_AGENT=
env CODEX_SANDBOX=
env CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=
env GEMINI_CLI=
env OPENCODE=

# The run every CI build below belongs to, and the store its locks live in.
env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=wow-look-at-my/consumer
env GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242
env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1
[!GOOS:windows] env LOCKS=file://$WORK/locks
[GOOS:windows]  env LOCKS=file:///$WORK/locks
[!GOOS:windows] env UNTOUCHED=file://$WORK/untouched
[GOOS:windows]  env UNTOUCHED=file:///$WORK/untouched
[!GOOS:windows] env BLOCKED=file://$WORK/blocked/locks
[GOOS:windows]  env BLOCKED=file:///$WORK/blocked/locks
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$LOCKS

cd $WORK/alpha
exec git init
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'alpha main'
exec git branch -m main

# beta imports alpha, and its own go.mod records the placeholder for it.
cd $WORK/beta
exec git init
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-02-02T03:04:05Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-02-02T03:04:05Z
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'beta main'
exec git branch -m main

# The first CI build of the run resolves each head, locks it, and records it in
# go.mod as any build does. A placeholder is no error.
cd $WORK/m
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=true
go run .
stdout '^alpha-main beta-main$'
grep '^	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-[0-9a-f]+$' go.mod
grep '^	github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0\.0\.0-20260202030405-[0-9a-f]+$' go.mod
exists $WORK/locks

# alpha moves while the run is under way.
cd $WORK/alpha
cp $WORK${/}alpha-next${/}alpha.go alpha.go
env GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-03T04:05:06Z
env GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-03T04:05:06Z
exec git commit -am 'alpha next'

# Another job of the same run, in its own checkout, builds the locked version
# and not the new head.
cd $WORK/m2
go run .
stdout '^alpha-main beta-main$'
go list -m github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
stdout '^github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260102030405-[0-9a-f]+$'
go build -o $WORK${/}m2${/}prog .
go version -m $WORK${/}m2${/}prog
stdout 'dep\tgithub.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha\tv0\.0\.0-20260102030405-[0-9a-f]+\th1:'

# A replace line takes the locked version too.
cd $WORK/replace
go run .
stdout '^alpha-main$'

# Outside CI the build follows the new head and never opens the store.
cd $WORK/m
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$UNTOUCHED
go run .
stdout '^alpha-next beta-main$'
grep '^	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0\.0\.0-20260103040506-[0-9a-f]+$' go.mod
! exists $WORK/untouched

# A coding agent does not make a CI build, whatever GITHUB_ACTIONS says.
cd $WORK/m2
env GITHUB_ACTIONS=true
env CLAUDECODE=1
go run .
stdout '^alpha-next beta-main$'
! exists $WORK/untouched
env CLAUDECODE=

# A new attempt of the run locks the heads again.
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$LOCKS
env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2
cd $WORK/fresh
go run .
stdout '^alpha-next beta-main$'
env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1

# A store the build cannot use fails the build. The error names the store and
# the module, and nothing stands in for the lock.
cd $WORK/placeholder
cp go.mod $WORK/placeholder.go.mod
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$BLOCKED
! go build ./...
stderr 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha@HEAD: run lock store file:.*blocked/locks: '
cmp go.mod $WORK/placeholder.go.mod

# A CI build that names no run has no lock to read, and fails the same way.
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$LOCKS
env GITHUB_RUN_ID=
! go build ./...
stderr 'github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha@HEAD: a CI build locks org modules per run, and GITHUB_RUN_ID is not set'
env GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242

# Vendor mode resolves nothing, so it never opens the store.
cd $WORK/vendor
env GOSMOPOLITAN_RUN_LOCK_STORE=$BLOCKED
go run .
stdout '^alpha-vendored$'

-- $WORK/home/gopher/.gitconfig --
[user]
	name = Go Gopher
	email = gopher@golang.org
-- $WORK/blocked --
a regular file, so no directory can sit under it
-- $WORK/alpha/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha

go 1.21
-- $WORK/alpha/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-main" }
-- $WORK/alpha-next/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-next" }
-- $WORK/beta/go.mod --
module github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/beta/beta.go --
package beta

import _ "github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"

func Name() string { return "beta-main" }
-- $WORK/m/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require (
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0.0.0
)
-- $WORK/m/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name(), beta.Name())
}
-- $WORK/m2/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require (
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0.0.0
)
-- $WORK/m2/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name(), beta.Name())
}
-- $WORK/fresh/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.21

require (
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
	github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta v0.0.0
)
-- $WORK/fresh/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/beta"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name(), beta.Name())
}
-- $WORK/replace/go.mod --
module example.com/replace

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0-20260102030405-0f69f837cebe

replace github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha => github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/replace/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/placeholder/go.mod --
module example.com/placeholder

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/placeholder/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/vendor/go.mod --
module example.com/vendored

go 1.21

require github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
-- $WORK/vendor/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(alpha.Name())
}
-- $WORK/vendor/vendor/modules.txt --
# github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha v0.0.0
## explicit; go 1.21
github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha
-- $WORK/vendor/vendor/github.com/wow-look-at-my/alpha/alpha.go --
package alpha

func Name() string { return "alpha-vendored" }
